result.note: The story reports Davos remarks rather than a policy decision, so it gets one statements question on the cited pollution-cost estimates.

questions.prompt: In January 2026, former IMF chief economist Gita Gopinath spoke about pollution at a Davos panel on India's growth. Consider the following statements about her remarks:
items: She said the economic damage from tariffs already outweighs that from pollution.
She cited a 2022 World Bank study estimating nearly 1.7 million pollution-linked deaths a year in India, about 18% of all deaths.
A 2021 study cited in the discussion estimated that air pollution costs Indian businesses about USD 95 billion annually, around 3% of GDP.
questions.ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 1 is wrong because Gopinath said the reverse: pollution's economic damage already outweighs the impact of tariffs. The other two figures are as reported, and she called for treating pollution control as a national mission on par with deregulation.
questions.source: Speaking at a panel on India’s growth trajectory, the former IMF chief economist said pollution’s economic damage already outweighs the impact of tariffs.
